newsitem.title: GERMANY: Munich airport plans 2nd passenger terminal.
newsitem.headline: Munich airport plans 2nd passenger terminal.

text.p: A second passenger terminal is to be built at Munich Airport (MUC) at a cost of up to 1.7 billion marks, airport authority Flughafen Muenchen GmbH (FMG) said.
The new terminal would have an initial capacity of 15 million passengers a year and could be opened in 2002 or 2003, FMG managing director Willi Hermsen said.
The current terminal, opened in 1992, was already approaching its limit of 18 million passengers as Munich developed into an international hub, he told a news conference.

Passenger numbers at Munich Airport rose 5.5 percent to a new record of 15.7 million in 1996 and Munich was now the country's second-largest airport behind Frankfurt and ahead of Duesseldorf, he added.
Transit passengers now represented 20 percent of total numbers, mostly due to the decision of Deutsche Lufthansa AG to develop its second German hub at Munich.

"Since the Lufthansa route expansion at Munich is in no way complete and the frequency of connecting and feeder flights will be increased, a further strengthening of the hub function can be expected in the coming years," Hermsen said.
"In view of the rapid traffic growth and Lufthansa hub plans, we must act now if we do not want to risk our excellent competitive position," he added.
The airport supervisory board had given the green light for a space and function plan and an architectural competition would be held this summer, he said.
Travellers using international flights to and from Munich increased 8.7 percent to 9.57 million last year, the authority said.
Demand for intercontinental flights, in particular, rose 15 percent to more than one million passengers, including a 33 percent rise to 145,000 passengers for North America.
European routes showed a plus of eight percent to more than six million passengers with Spain, Britain, Italy, Greece and France as the most popular destinations.
Passenger numbers on domestic flights, however, rose only 1.0 percent to 5.87 million.
